headline: Stop asking questions in your hooks.
proof: Statements stop the scroll. Questions let people decide they don't care.
caption:
Most videos lose people in the first 2 seconds because the hook sounds optional.

"Wanna know how?" lets people scroll.
"Your first 2 seconds are killing your views" makes them stop.

Tease, don't ask. A statement creates tension a question never will.

headline: Every viral video has 3 acts.
proof: Hook, then tension, then payoff. Skip the middle and retention dies.
caption:
Every short-form video that pops has 3 acts:

1. Hook (0 to 1.5s) — state the problem sharp
2. Tension (4 to 12s) — give a reason to stay
3. Payoff (13s to end) — deliver, then one clear close

Most people film all hook or all payoff. The tension in the middle is what holds people.

headline: Your B-roll is boring.

Verbs: someone doing the task, wide and busy.
Nouns: the object itself, close-up, isolated, lit.

B-roll wins on detail, not motion. Get tight on the noun.

headline: A great hook plants ONE question.
subheadline: If viewers ask different things, you lost them.
proof: If 1,000 people watch your first line, all 1,000 should be asking the same question.
caption:
Your hook has one job: put a single question in every viewer's head.

"Here are 3 ways I grew last year" — grew what? Followers? Money? Muscle? Everyone builds a different story, and the second your next line doesn't match theirs, they scroll.

"3 ways business owners grow faster on Reels" — one subject, one question: what are they?

One subject. One question. Then answer it.

headline: The visual IS the hook.
proof: Eyes process 10-100x more per second than ears. Your first frame decides before your first word lands.
caption:
Stop writing hooks first. Pick the visual first.

Viewers process your video in this order: see the visual → hear your words → look back at the visual to confirm. If the frame, the words, and the on-screen text don't say the same thing, their brain stalls — and they scroll.

So before you script anything, ask: what's the single most interesting thing I can SHOW in the first 2 seconds?

Then write the words to match it. Add a 3-5 word text overlay that says the same thing.

All three aligned = they stay.

headline: Say "but" more. Say "and then" never.
subheadline: Contrast keeps people watching. Lists put them to sleep.
proof: If "and then" fits between your sentences, the story is flat. "But" and "therefore" create tension.
caption:
The fastest script fix that exists:

Read your script. Everywhere two sentences connect with "and then" — energy, gone. The brain already guessed what's next, so it checks out.

Rewrite so the beats connect with "but" or "therefore."

"He opened a second location AND THEN hired 4 barbers" → flat.
"He opened a second location, BUT nobody showed up. THEREFORE he tried one thing..." → now you need to know.

Drop a "but" every 20 seconds and watch your retention graph change shape.

Follow @josephborroto for script fixes like this.

#scriptwriting #storytelling #shortformvideo #reelstips #audienceretention #josephborroto

headline: Stop inventing video ideas from scratch.
proof: The best predictor of a winning video is a video that already won. Remix it — don't reinvent it.
caption:
Making up ideas from your head is content on hard mode.

Every niche already has proof: videos that did 10x that channel's normal views. Those aren't luck — they're validated ideas.

Once a week, spend one hour:
→ List 15-20 accounts in your niche.
→ Find their outliers (way above their average).
→ Note the topic, the hook, the format.
→ Keep what worked, swap in your story, your niche, your proof.

Change it enough to make it yours. That's not copying — that's how every great creator you follow does it.

headline: Ship it at a 7. Not a 10.
subheadline: Volume builds the skill that quality needs.
proof: You can win with a 9/10 video. You'll never post enough 10s to matter.
caption:
Perfectionism is just procrastination with better branding.

The play:
1. Get your videos to a 7/10 — good, with a couple things you know could be better.
2. Lock in the volume: one a day for short-form.
3. THEN push quality toward a 9 — which happens on its own, because reps build the skill.

Posting one "perfect" video a month loses to posting daily at a 7 every single time. The algorithm rewards the reps, and so does your skill curve.

Done and posted beats perfect.
